thread_analysis.thread_summary: An internal exchange between [COMPANY] staff reports RF test results for [COMPANY]'s UXC10 module, where all RF test items passed except one (RF/TRM/CA), which had been included in the Test Plan only as a precaution because it was unclear whether the DUT supported the optional Enhanced Power Control feature. The DUT's own test log response explicitly indicated non-support for this feature, resolving the ambiguity. The consultant instructs that this item be excluded from scope and removed from the log so the RF report can be finalized, and asks for the Test Plan to be updated accordingly.
all_questions_found: Since it was unclear whether the DUT supports Enhanced Power Control, how should the one RF test item that did not pass be handled given the DUT's own log response indicates non-support for that feature?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A DUT's own protocol-level response during an RF test item can resolve an upfront ambiguity about whether it supports an optional feature; if the DUT explicitly responds as not supporting the feature, the corresponding test item is excluded from scope rather than treated as a failure.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: When a test item was only included in the Test Plan as a precaution due to uncertainty about optional feature support, and the DUT's own log response during that test explicitly confirms non-support, the item should be marked out of scope and removed from both the log and the final report rather than counted as a non-pass.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Treating this item as a failed test result instead of an out-of-scope item would incorrectly suggest the DUT failed a test it was never required to support, and would require correcting the Test Plan, log, and RF report afterward.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a test item is included in a Test Plan only as a precaution against uncertain optional feature support, check the DUT's own protocol response within that test's log before treating a non-pass as a failure -- an explicit non-support response from the DUT means the item should be excluded from scope, not counted against the product.
